Or will water violently carried off by the wind turn aside? Something of the same kind that line of Vergil also sounds: Sooner, therefore, shall the nimble stags graze in the air, and the seas leave the fishes bare upon the shore, than his face shall slip from our heart; and in another place: While rivers run into the seas, while shadows move over the slopes of the mountains, while the sky feeds the stars, ever shall your honor, your name and your praises abide. 'Just as,' he says, 'the snow cannot fail from the summits of Lebanon, nor is it overcome by any heat of the sun so as to melt entirely, and the streams flowing down from the mountains are by no means dried up at their springs, so my name, which is in itself stable and everlasting, cannot be changed; and yet, while all other things keep the order of nature, my people has forgotten me.' For there follows:

"For my people have forgotten me, they have burned incense in vain." Everyone who sins has forgotten God, but the righteous one says, "All these things have come upon us, and we have not forgotten you, nor have we done wrong" — and he burned incense in vain. But what "they have burned incense in vain" means must be considered. If we take up again the things said earlier upon the hundred and fortieth Psalm, we shall understand what "they have burned incense in vain" is. Now there was in the Psalm something of this sort said: "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before you." Therefore my prayer, being composed of a fine heart — when our heart is not made gross — being sent up, becomes as incense before God. If, then, the prayer of the righteous is incense before God, the prayer of the unrighteous is indeed incense, but such incense that it may be said concerning it and concerning the unrighteous who prays, "they have burned incense in vain"; as is written concerning Judas, "Let his prayer become sin." That man, in his praying, burned incense in vain. And who it is that burns incense in vain, let us consider still further in this way. "Three times in the year," it says, "shall every male of yours appear before the Lord your God," to which is immediately added, "You shall not appear before me empty."

For my people has forgotten me, making libations in vain and stumbling in their ways, in the paths of the age — or everlasting —, so that they walked in them on a road not trodden. He who forgets God and forsakes him who says: I am the way, and pours libations to strange gods, stumbles in his own ways — not God's at all, but his own — and forsakes the ancient and everlasting paths, which are trodden by the footprints of all the saints who worship God. These, however, have walked on a road not trodden and, having abandoned the worship of God, have venerated idols; on account of which the punishment that follows is brought upon them:

So that their land should become a desolation and an everlasting hissing; everyone who passes by it shall be astonished and shall shake his head. 'And because they have forsaken,' he says, 'the worship of God and have followed the depraved paths of idolatry, therefore their land has been reduced to a wilderness and to a wonder and a hissing to all, so that those who saw the land and city, once most flourishing, collapsed into a desert and ashes should marvel and be astonished and show the confusion of their soul by the gesture of their body'; for this is what it is to shake the head and to show the astonishment of the mind by hissing. And this we understand to have been fulfilled more fully and more correctly after the coming of the Lord, when none of the Jews is permitted by law to enter the land and the once holy city; but when they come to mourn, they marvel at and weep over the prophecies of the prophets fulfilled in deed.

Like a burning wind I will scatter them before the enemy — or the enemies —; the back and not the face will I show them in the day of their perdition. To this day the sentence of God remains upon the Jews; they have been scattered throughout the whole world before the enemy, the devil, or the enemies, the demons, and, though day and night in the synagogues of Satan they call upon the name of God, God shows them his back and not his face, so that they may understand that he is always withdrawing and never coming to them. Now the day of the perdition of the Jews is the whole time after the Savior's passion until the consummation of the age, so that, after the fullness of the nations has come in, then all Israel may be saved.

And they said: Come and let us devise devices against Jeremiah! For the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet; come and let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not heed all his words! This was both then the thought of the Jews against Jeremiah, or against the Lord the Savior, and is today the thought of heretics against his servants: to contrive calumnies and to forestall holy men with accusation, and not to consider what truth those men speak, but what falsehood they themselves may contrive; for they boast that the law of God and counsel and utterance remain in their own priests and wise men and false prophets, though Scripture says: Into a perverse soul wisdom shall not enter.

Attend to me, O Lord, and hear the voice of my adversaries! Is evil repaid for good, that they have dug a pit for my soul? Remember that I stood in your sight to speak good for them and to turn away your indignation from them! Therefore give their children up to famine and lead them into the hands of the sword; let their wives be childless and widows, and let their husbands be put to death, let their young men be pierced by the sword in battle, let an outcry be heard from their houses! In the type of the Savior, indeed, Jeremiah suffers all these things from the people of the Jews, who were afterwards laid waste when the Babylonian came; but they are fulfilled more fully and more perfectly in Christ. And when the city was overthrown they were slaughtered by the Roman sword, not because of idolatry, which did not exist at that time, but because of the killing of the Son of God, when the whole people together cried out: Away, away with such a man; we have no king but Caesar! And their imprecation has been fulfilled by everlasting damnation: His blood be upon us and upon our children! For they had dug a pit for Christ and had said: Let us take him away from the land of the living! — he who had such great mercy toward them, and stood in the sight of the Father to speak good for them and to turn away his indignation from them, that on the cross also he said: Father, forgive them! For they do not know what they are doing. We pass quickly over what is plain, so as to linger on the more obscure passages, by no means following the ravings of certain people who interpret this even of a captivity of the heavenly Jerusalem, but pursuing the clear history and the most manifest prophecy with all confidence in the words and the senses.

For you will bring a robber upon them suddenly, because they have dug a pit to catch me and have hidden snares for my feet. But you, O Lord, know all their counsel against me unto death; do not be propitious to their iniquity, and let their sin not be blotted out from before your face; let them be falling — or stumbling — in your sight; in the time of your fury consume them or deal with them! If we understand it of Jeremiah, let us refer the sudden robber to Nebuchadnezzar; if of the Savior, which is truer and better, to the Roman army. And lest the sentence of God should seem unjust, he sets out what they did against Christ, the Son of God, and what they suffered.

But what he adds: do not be propitious to their iniquity, and let their sin not be blotted out from before your face, is by no means contrary to the earlier sentence, in which he entreats the Father for the people; but after the time given for repentance has passed and they persevere in their crime, they are punished not so much for themselves as for others, lest a sin left unpunished should harm the rest by its example. And what he adds: let them be stumbling — or falling — in your sight, is like that saying of Isaiah and of the apostle Peter: and you shall not stumble as on a stone of offense and a rock of scandal; which the prophet also mentions in the psalms: The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner; this was done by the Lord.
